accessible_name: Definition of a closed theory and its closure
listen_text: Definition: Gamma is closed when every sentence semantically entailed by Gamma already belongs to Gamma. The closure of Gamma is the set of every sentence it semantically entails. Gamma is axiomatized by Delta when Gamma is Delta's closure.
long_description: The definition relates closure under semantic consequence to axiomatization by a sentence set.
ordered_steps: Definition: Gamma is closed when every sentence semantically entailed by Gamma already belongs to Gamma.
The closure of Gamma is the set of every sentence it semantically entails.
Gamma is axiomatized by Delta when Gamma is Delta's closure.

accessible_name: Definition of a model of a sentence set
listen_text: Definition: structure M is a model of Gamma exactly when M satisfies every sentence A that belongs to Gamma.
long_description: The definition gives the truth condition for a structure to model Gamma.
ordered_steps: Definition: structure M is a model of Gamma exactly when M satisfies every sentence A that belongs to Gamma.

listen_text: Example: the universal reflexivity, antisymmetry, and transitivity sentences have exactly the structures whose interpreted less-than-or-equal relation is a partial order.
long_description: The example matches three first-order sentences with reflexivity antisymmetry and transitivity.
ordered_steps: Example: the universal reflexivity, antisymmetry, and transitivity sentences have exactly the structures whose interpreted less-than-or-equal relation is a partial order.

listen_text: Displayed axiom set: every x is below itself. If x is below y and y is below x, then x equals y. If x is below y and y is below z, then x is below z.
long_description: The display lists the three sentences defining a partial order.
ordered_steps: Displayed axiom set: every x is below itself.
If x is below y and y is below x, then x equals y.
If x is below y and y is below z, then x is below z.

accessible_name: Example theory of strict linear orders
listen_text: Example: less than is irreflexive, total on distinct objects, and transitive. Every strict linear order is a model, and every strict linear order relation on X determines a model with domain X.
long_description: The example states the strict-order axioms and constructs a corresponding model from any strict linear order.
ordered_steps: Example: less than is irreflexive, total on distinct objects, and transitive.
Every strict linear order is a model, and every strict linear order relation on X determines a model with domain X.

listen_text: Displayed axiom set: no x is less than itself. For every x and y, x is less than y, y is less than x, or they are equal. Less than is transitive.
long_description: The display lists irreflexivity totality and transitivity.
ordered_steps: Displayed axiom set: no x is less than itself.
For every x and y, x is less than y, y is less than x, or they are equal.
Less than is transitive.

listen_text: Example: every x times one equals x, multiplication is associative, and every x has a y such that x times y equals one.
long_description: The example presents identity associativity and inverse axioms.
ordered_steps: Example: every x times one equals x, multiplication is associative, and every x has a y such that x times y equals one.

listen_text: Displayed axioms: right identity by one; associativity of multiplication; and existence of a right inverse for each object.

ordered_steps: Displayed axioms: right identity by one; associativity of multiplication; and existence of a right inverse for each object.

listen_text: Example: successor is injective and never zero. Addition and multiplication satisfy their zero and successor recursions. Less than is defined by positive difference. Every formula A contributes its induction instance.

ordered_steps: Example: successor is injective and never zero.
Addition and multiplication satisfy their zero and successor recursions.

accessible_name: Example candidate theory of pure sets
listen_text: Example: a proposed pure-set theory asserts empty set, extensionality, pairing, union, and unrestricted comprehension. Taking A of y to mean that y is not an element of itself yields a sentence satisfied by no structure.

ordered_steps: Example: a proposed pure-set theory asserts empty set, extensionality, pairing, union, and unrestricted comprehension.

listen_text: Displayed axioms: an empty set exists; any two sets with the same elements are equal; pair sets exist; unions exist; and for every formula A there is a set containing exactly its satisfying objects.
long_description: The display lists four ordinary set axioms and the unrestricted comprehension schema.
ordered_steps: Displayed axioms: an empty set exists; any two sets with the same elements are equal; pair sets exist; unions exist; and for every formula A there is a set containing exactly its satisfying objects.

listen_text: Example: parthood is reflexive, antisymmetric, and transitive. In addition, any two objects have a mereological sum characterized as their least common whole.

ordered_steps: Example: parthood is reflexive, antisymmetric, and transitive.

listen_text: Displayed axioms: every object is part of itself; mutual parthood implies identity; parthood is transitive; and every x and y have a z whose superobjects are exactly their common superobjects.
long_description: The display gives reflexivity antisymmetry transitivity and the sum principle.
ordered_steps: Displayed axioms: every object is part of itself; mutual parthood implies identity; parthood is transitive; and every x and y have a z whose superobjects are exactly their common superobjects.

accessible_name: Definition of a formula expressing a relation
listen_text: Definition: formula A with free variables v sub one through v sub n expresses relation R in structure M exactly when R holds of a sub one through a sub n if and only if M satisfies A under every assignment sending each v sub i to a sub i.
long_description: The definition connects free variables assignments tuples and satisfaction.
ordered_steps: Definition: formula A with free variables v sub one through v sub n expresses relation R in structure M exactly when R holds of a sub one through a sub n if and only if M satisfies A under every assignment sending each v sub i to a sub i.

ordered_steps: Example: arithmetic formulas express less than or equal to, successor, predecessor, and strict less than in the standard natural-number structure.

accessible_name: Proposition expressing at least and at most n elements
listen_text: Proposition: A sub at least n asserts the existence of n pairwise distinct domain elements. It is true exactly when the domain has at least n elements. The negation of A sub at least n plus one is true exactly when the domain has at most n elements.
long_description: The proposition defines A sub at least n and relates its negation to an upper bound.
ordered_steps: Proposition: A sub at least n asserts the existence of n pairwise distinct domain elements.
It is true exactly when the domain has at least n elements.
The negation of A sub at least n plus one is true exactly when the domain has at most n elements.

accessible_name: Displayed sentence for at least n elements

long_description: The display existentially binds n objects and requires every pair to be distinct.
ordered_steps: Displayed definition: choose x sub one through x sub n and require all distinctness comparisons, continuing through x sub n minus one not equal to x sub n.

listen_text: Proposition: A sub exactly n asserts the existence of n pairwise distinct objects and says every domain object equals one of them. It is true exactly in structures with n elements.
